answers.answer: Did a fresh targeted WebSearch check for both (I don't share signals' FMP/INDmoney outage -- WebSearch was available). GOOG: no acute same-day (09-23) headline found. The closest dated, sourced mechanism is from 09-22: GOOG failed at $360 resistance and fell back near $350 as investors weigh the FY26 capex guide ($180-190bn) and negative Q2 free cash flow (-$5.9bn) against Gemini engagement growth ('Gemini growth meets spending concerns') -- a continuing capex/monetization-worry narrative, not a fresh shock. That explains direction and rough scale (~-2.8% in the cited round-trip) but not the FULL -3.5% today: GOOG's move is ~5x the broad tech tape (SPX -0.69%, NDX -0.68% today), so some idiosyncratic component is still unaccounted for by anything I found. Read it as continuation of an existing capex-overhang concern amplified by today's broad softness, not a new named catalyst on top-up day -- I don't have a smoking gun and won't invent one. CIEN: this corroborates, not just repeats, the mean-reversion/technical read from the first stop-out. Multiple independent sources describe the SAME pattern -- CIEN sliding 'despite overwhelmingly positive company news' (fresh optical/AI-infra contract wins, backlog $7.7bn, FY guide raised to ~$6.3bn) -- i.e. profit-taking/multiple-compression after a strong run, not fundamental deterioration. One more factor specific to a SECOND stop-out in two sessions: CIEN's position is dust-sized (0.01% weight, ~$2.98, already flagged elsewhere for a re-establish-or-zero decision), so ordinary volatility on a near-zero-dollar position will trip a tight stop repeatedly almost by construction -- that's a sizing artifact, not new bearish evidence, and I'd weight it accordingly.
